clue.text: Good time follows single and double

indicators.note: follows tells the solver that the piece for good comes after the piece for single

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for single
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tennis player's good spell follows winning a singles match and a doubles one.
explanation.walkthrough: S + PI + T gives SPIT; 'Good time' reads as a phrase but splits into two pieces placed after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's spit, as in 'the spit and image', is their exact likeness or lookalike.

clue.text: Failure of power gives rise to censorship

blocks.note: first meaning: an electricity cut leaving everything dark
second meaning: a suppression of news or information

explanation.surface: A power cut leads the authorities to suppress the news.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a loss of electrical supply and an official ban on reporting, as in a media blackout.

clue.text: Weapons and gifts exchanging hands

indicators.note: left and right are the two hands, so one hand's letter is traded for the other's

blocks.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: Weapons and presents being handed from one person to another.
explanation.walkthrough: In ALMS the L (left) is swapped for R (right), giving ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms is the standard collective word for guns and other weapons of war.

clue.text: Enthusiasts choose to enter river and start to swim

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the word for choose sits within the river
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to vote is to choose at the ballot box
the opening letter of swim

explanation.surface: Keen swimmers pick a river to plunge into and begin swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a common crossword river; there are rivers of that name in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotees are ardent followers or fans of something, the same as enthusiasts.

clue.text: 1,000,000 donkeys – that's loads …

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for a million
asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: A million donkeys would certainly be a lot of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which also builds its answer from numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Masses, like loads, is an informal plural meaning a great quantity of something.

clue.text: … 10001000 story is similar?

blocks.note: split as 100, 0 and 1000: Roman C, the letter O, and Roman M
a parable is a moral story

explanation.surface: A puzzling string of digits, then a question whether some tale resembles another.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit string looks like binary but splits into 100, 0 and 1000, read as Roman numerals and a letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are comparable can be likened to each other, being alike in kind or degree.

clue.text: Promote book: 'Egypt on Vacation'

indicators.note: a place on vacation has been vacated, emptied of everything but its edges

blocks.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament
the word emptied, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Publicising a travel book titled Egypt on Vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To market a product is to advertise and sell it, which is to promote it.

clue.text: Support or prohibit defending base

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to bar is to prohibit
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A choice between backing or banning the defence of a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the mathematical constant used as the base of natural logs, sits inside BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a weight is to hold it up, so it means to support.

clue.text: Extract money from tooth after Penny's opposed

indicators.note: to extract is to pull something out, so a letter is removed
after says the shortened tooth is placed behind the coin

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
M is short for money
a molar is a back tooth

explanation.surface: A dentist pulls a tooth for money, against the wishes of someone called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' and 'tooth' suggest dentistry, but extract is the instruction to remove a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar describes things at opposite extremes, such as polar views that are directly contrary.

clue.text: English party talk is complicated

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Lab is short for the Labour Party
to orate is to talk formally

explanation.surface: Political speeches by an English party are hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour, a major British political party, is abbreviated Lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate has many intricate parts, so it is involved and complicated.

clue.text: Henry's wearing odd socks, put to selling shoelaces here?

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so those letters are rearranged
someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry has mismatched socks on and is set to work selling laces for shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoelaces here are liquorice laces, a sweet sold in British school tuck shops, which are snack shops for pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck shop is a school snack kiosk that sells sweets such as liquorice shoelaces.

clue.text: Game played beside the fire?

blocks.note: first meaning: a card game with betting
second meaning: the metal rod kept by the hearth to stir coals

explanation.surface: A cosy card game by the fireside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gambling card game and the iron rod kept next to a fireplace for stirring embers.

clue.text: Stock market activity performed under the table

blocks.note: first meaning: the colloquial name for the FTSE 100 share index
second meaning: flirtatious touching of feet out of sight

explanation.surface: Shady share dealing done in secret, under the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The FTSE 100, the main London share index, is nicknamed the Footsie.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the nickname of London's leading share index and a flirtatious game of touching feet.

clue.text: Able to eat trout regularly with food

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
what is eaten goes inside, so the kept letters go into the word for able

blocks.note: fit means able or capable
second and fourth letters of the fish

explanation.surface: Someone well enough to eat trout as a regular part of their diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit is a category of food, so the general word stands for a particular kind.

clue.text: Russia repelled, firmly established without capital being hemmed in

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the abbreviation is read backwards
the capital is the opening letter, and without says it is dropped

blocks.note: RUS is the international code for Russia
a grounded belief is firmly established

explanation.surface: Russia is pushed back and its entrenched forces end up encircled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city such as Moscow; here it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surrounded is to be enclosed on every side, which is what hemmed in means.

clue.text: Mark's a player with no handicap

blocks.note: first meaning: a thin line scored on a surface
second meaning: a golfer who plays off zero

explanation.surface: A golfer called Mark plays off zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' reads as a man's name; it is the first definition, with 's standing for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a shallow score on a surface and, in golf, a player whose handicap is zero.

clue.text: Dear Mel …

blocks.note: first meaning: a term of endearment for a loved one
second meaning: the Latin and pharmacy word for the sweet stuff bees make

explanation.walkthrough: Mel looks like a person's name being addressed; it is Latin for the bees' product, still used in pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an affectionate address like darling and the sweet food bees make, called mel in Latin.

clue.text: Chief of Police thrown out of club, say

indicators.note: someone thrown out is expelled, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: the leading letter of police
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is expelled from a members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is a golf club, not a society; dropping its first P leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak it aloud, so the verb means to say.

clue.text: Deep 23 evenly flowing west

indicators.note: evenly picks out the letters in the even-numbered places
in an across answer west is leftward, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the answer to 23 down, its second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Deep water flowing calmly westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is WATERS, so its even letters are A, E and S. 'The deep' is a poetic name for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a literary term for the open ocean, so it stands for the sea.

clue.text: … most annoyed doctor rang – it's about tablet

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so those letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the drug

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A furious patient phoned the doctor complaining about some pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person who rang; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Angriest is the superlative of angry, so it means the most annoyed or cross.

clue.text: Toast bread

blocks.note: first meaning: to colour food under heat
second meaning: a wholemeal loaf

explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast bread' reads as an instruction to the cook; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To brown food is to toast it under heat, and brown is also the name for wholemeal bread.

clue.text: Cryptically, draws in a direction away from port

definitions.text: in a direction away from port

blocks.note: this word says the answer is itself a clue, whose first part is a jumbling instruction
the word the answer's own reading produces

explanation.surface: A ship heading out of harbour, described in a puzzling way.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as a clue, and OUT is an anagram signal applied to WARDS, which yields draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwards means moving away from a centre, so a ship going outwards is leaving port.

clue.text: Perfectly holding body of fighters with tug

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to a T means perfectly
the World Boxing Organization, a governing body for boxers

explanation.surface: Boxers perfectly holding their bodies while in a tug of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of fighters' suggests a physique; it is a boxing governing body, the World Boxing Organization.
explanation.definitionFit: A towboat is a vessel that pulls or pushes other craft, which is what a tug does.

clue.text: Wife rates sexy member of Pink Floyd

indicators.note: sexy suggests something hot and stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife judges one of the rock band's members attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Waters was the bassist and a principal songwriter of the band Pink Floyd.

clue.text: One sampling bit of salsa covered in potato

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece, here its opening letter
covered in means wrapped by, so that letter goes inside the potato word

blocks.note: tater is informal for potato
the opening letter of salsa

explanation.surface: Someone trying a dab of salsa smeared on a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a person who tries food or drink to judge it, so someone sampling.

clue.text: Striped pastel covered in shade to a large extent

indicators.note: stripes alternate, so every other letter is kept
covered in means wrapped by, so the kept letters go inside the colour word

blocks.note: grey is a shade of colour
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A striped pastel fabric mostly hidden under a darker shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatly is an adverb meaning very much, which is the same as to a large extent.

clue.text: Very fond of husband's orange top, not pants

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter
pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the opening letter of orange
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone adores their husband's orange shirt but not his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers or underwear; it is British slang for rubbish, used to signal the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hot on something is an informal idiom for being keen on or enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Mercury eclipsing face of Uranus and Earth? That's immense

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its opening letter
an eclipsing body passes in front and covers another, so one piece encloses the letter

blocks.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
the opening letter of the planet
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Planets lining up in an eclipse, with Earth asked if it is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercury looks like the planet; it is the metal, whose symbol Hg goes round U before E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge describes something extremely large, so it is a direct synonym of immense.

clue.text: I'm stopping horrible racists with swords

indicators.note: horrible suggests something ugly and mangled, so those letters are rearranged
stopping a gap means plugging it, so the short word goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vigilante vows to halt armed bigots.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, so the plural names a kind of swords.

clue.text: 10 across taking time – hint?

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the short piece goes into the others

blocks.note: the digits 1 and 0 read as the letters I and O
T is the abbreviation for time
A is the abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: A solver asks whether 10 across gives a clue to what time it is.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 across' looks like a cross-reference to another clue; it is read literally as IO and A, with T placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a tiny amount, like a hint or trace of something.

clue.text: Island broadcaster on air

indicators.note: on air means being broadcast, heard rather than read

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A TV company broadcasting live from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland; Sky is a British pay-TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides in Scotland, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: They tend flowers Ivan oddly swapped with queen

indicators.note: oddly picks out the letters in the odd-numbered places
swapped with says one set of letters is taken out and another put in its place

blocks.note: gardenias are fragrant white flowers
first and third letters of the name
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Florists named Ivan oddly traded places with a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They tend flowers' looks like the whole definition, but flowers is the wordplay; IA in GARDENIAS becomes ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners are people who look after plants and plots, so they are those who tend.

clue.text: Still taking days returning toy

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the days go within the first word
returning means going back, so the whole is read in reverse

blocks.note: still and yet both mean even so
D is the abbreviation for day, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A child keeps the same toy for days on end, always coming back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a stuffed toy bear, so it is a particular kind of toy.
